items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to procedures involving taxpayer interviews
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3956

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to procedures
involving taxpayer interviews

PURPOSE:

Ensures that when taxpayers are represented by an Enrolled Agent on
State tax matters, the NYS Department of Taxation and Finance will
only communicate with the taxpayer through the taxpayer's Enrolled
Agent.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends subdivision (c) of section 3006 of the tax law to
add new language forbidding the Department of Taxation and Finance
from communicating with a taxpayer (by phone or in person) over the
collection of any unpaid tax if the Department knows that the taxpayer
is represented by a person authorized to practice before the US
Internal Revenue Service.

Section 2: Establishes the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

An Enrolled Agent is an authorized tax preparer licensed to practice
and represent clients before the federal Internal Revenue Service
(IRS). They also represent New York State taxpayers on state tax
issues. The clients of Enrolled Agents often sign "powers of attorney"
authorizing their representation and directing the IRS to send all
communications through the Enrolled Agent. Federal law and regulation
requires the IRS to communicate exclusively through the Enrolled
Agent, and requires the IRS to respect those "powers of attorney".

In New York, Enrolled Agents have had difficulty with the NYS
Department of Taxation and Finance respecting "powers of attorney",
and continuing to communicate directly with the represented taxpayer.
This leads to frustration and mistrust with both Enrolled Agents
working in New York and their clients. It can also delay the
resolution of these matters. This legislation makes it clear that if a
taxpayer is represented by an Enrolled Agent, the Department of
Taxation and Finance must only communicate with the taxpayer through
their agent. This bill makes exceptions if the taxpayer consents to
direct communication, or fails to respond in a timely manner with the
Department.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediately
